tasks.short: Attend shows and review fashion sources

steps.what: Attend fashion shows and observe garments and audience responses
Find and review garment magazines and manuals for trends and preferences
Capture selected references and actual observations in the collection reference board
Judge which trends and consumer preferences matter for the collection

tasks.design: Configure publication, season and topic filters for the existing fashion-source library in {DOCS}. Keep show attendance, substantive reading, first reference-board capture and interpretation with the designer; the view only reduces repeated source navigation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the relevant issue or season can repeat, while evaluating fashion still requires direct observation and reading.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document filters can use existing publication metadata without summarising garments or consumer preferences.
tasks.still_hard: A show or magazine is a selective signal and does not establish broad demand.
tasks.human_edge: The designer reads materials, context and cultural signals beyond a source index.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less library navigation; show attendance and design judgement are unchanged.

reach.task: Interpret market references for a design brief
reach.learn: Source selection and distinguishing observations from market assumptions

evidence.claim: Native source-library filters can reduce repeated issue and topic navigation; this is model knowledge, not measured fashion-research savings.

assumptions: Boundary is actual trend research including an existing collection reference board used in later design. No extra attendance report, consumer survey or new research-summary record is invented.

Publishers supply publication, issue date, season and source title where indexed. The designer first captures selected references and observations in s3. Missing source metadata or paper-only manuals are handled manually within retained s2 time.

Test native library filtering first. Three of thirty review hours are repeated issue and topic navigation; twenty-seven hours of reading and source assessment remain. All first capture and any ordinary author save within s3 remain ungated and unchanged.
There is no automatic summary, consumer-preference inference or source licensing assumption.
unknowns: Whether source navigation is already efficient
Whether the designer actually keeps a reference board
research_questions: Does a native season filter remove navigation while preserving access to original pages?

already_counted.description: Read the actual sources and first capture selected collection references

incremental.description: Maintain library filter fields and source links

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: three navigation hours removed less 0.5 upkeep gives 2.5. Cautious case: this season's sources are print-only or lack usable season metadata, retaining all thirty review hours; the extra filter is not deployed or maintained. Show attendance, first observation capture and interpretation retain all their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Purchase clothing and accessories to complete designs

steps.what: Identify which clothing or accessory item the design requires
Check existing sample stock for a suitable item
Visit sellers or search listings for suitable new or used items
Inspect candidate items for condition, fit and design suitability
Confirm the exact item, seller, price and purchase conditions
Purchase the checked clothing or accessory item from the seller
File the actual purchase receipt for reimbursement or accounts
First record the acquired item and its location in sample stock

tasks.design: Configure native item-type and location filters in the {OTHER} sample-stock record system to shorten checking existing items before buying. Keep seller visits, condition checks, purchase selection, the actual payment and first receipt and stock capture with the designer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding existing sample items can require several stock views; used-item condition and suitability still need inspection.
tasks.enabler_now: Native stock filters can expose already recorded item and location fields.
tasks.still_hard: A visually similar item may have the wrong fit, construction or condition.
tasks.human_edge: The designer recognises when a purchased item will actually complete the design.
tasks.altitude: Less searching in recorded stock; sourcing and purchase judgement remain the same.

reach.task: Source suitable physical props within a design budget
reach.learn: Condition inspection and clear item provenance

evidence.claim: Native inventory filters can reduce navigation through existing stock records; this is model knowledge, not evidence that used-item selection can be automated.

assumptions: Boundary includes an actual purchase and the existing receipt and sample records used by accounts and designers. No automatic order, reimbursement approval, new stock report or assumed recurring procurement administration is introduced.

The designer or stock keeper already records item identifier, type, size and location for actual samples. Missing or inaccurate fields require manual checking within the seven retained s2 hours. The designer first enters each newly acquired item in s8, with all ten hours retained.
Test native stock filters first. Three of ten stock-lookup hours are repeated navigation; all physical inspection, seller search, condition judgement and first capture remain.

The exact item and purchase terms exist before s5; that check gates the one-hour real purchase action in s6. Receipt filing and ordinary author saves in s7 and s8 have no self-approval gate and no saving. No existing checkout runtime is banked as saved labour.
unknowns: Whether a usable sample-stock record exists
research_questions: Can existing stock filters shorten lookup without adding a new inventory-capture duty?

already_counted.description: Read stock details, inspect the exact purchase and check terms

incremental.description: Check sample-stock filter fields after changes

approvals.approved_version: Exact clothing or accessory item, seller, price and purchase terms checked in s5; changes require a fresh check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: three stock-navigation hours removed less 0.3 upkeep gives 2.7. Cautious case: unrecorded vintage samples require direct physical searching, retaining all ten stock-check hours; no extra filter is maintained. No sourcing trip, inspection, purchase, receipt capture or first stock entry is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Visit textile showrooms to learn about fabrics

steps.what: Travel to textile showrooms for the relevant fabric collections
Visit textile displays and inspect the latest fabrics' handle and drape
Discuss fabric composition, availability and collection suitability with showroom staff
Label selected swatches with their actual source and fabric details

tasks.design: Keep showroom visits, fabric handling and discussion with the designer. Reuse a native {DOCS} swatch-label template only for repeated label headings and layout, while first entering and verifying the actual supplier and fabric details.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical fabric qualities cannot be inferred from an index, though swatch labels repeat a small layout.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing label templates can remove blank-heading and layout preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Handle, drape, finish and suitability must be experienced directly.
tasks.human_edge: The designer compares tactile qualities with the collection's intended construction and look.
tasks.altitude: Essentially the same showroom work, with slightly less label layout.

reach.task: Inspect physical material samples for a design
reach.learn: Material provenance and translating tactile observations into design choices

evidence.claim: Native label templates can reuse headings without creating new fabric facts; this is model knowledge, not a measured showroom case.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual labelled swatches retained for collection material selection. No new visit report, showroom appointment administration or recurring trend log is invented.

Supplier labels and staff provide supplier name, fabric reference, composition and availability where known. The designer first enters and verifies those details in s4; missing details remain manual and are not supplied by a model.
Test native labels first. Only one of ten label hours is repeated blank-heading and layout work; nine first-capture and verification hours remain. Ordinary author saving has no gate or saving.
No trip or physical inspection is replaced by a digital catalogue.
unknowns: Whether the designer already uses a label template
research_questions: Is any repeat label layout left after using supplier-provided sample labels?

already_counted.description: First enter and verify the real swatch details

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: one label-layout hour removed less 0.2 upkeep gives 0.8. Cautious case: supplier labels already contain the needed fields or custom labels need all ten hours; no additional template is maintained. Travel, physical fabric inspection and discussion retain all ninety hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Adapt design ideas for the mass market

steps.what: Read the target market, price and production brief
Examine reference ideas and identify useful design principles
Choose original adaptations that fit the intended market and production limits
Draw and revise adapted garment concepts for the mass market

loop.purpose: Produce rough visual alternatives within the designer's entered direction
loop.input: Designer-written adaptation direction, silhouette constraints and authorised references
loop.output: Editable rough concept images with generation metadata retained
loop.check: Designer compares proportions, intended changes, originality and brief fit, rejecting visual details that imply unsupported construction
loop.stop: Two draft rounds maximum; unsuitable or overly similar images return to manual drawing; no technical pattern or production release
loop.why_not_simpler: Native drawing templates help repeated layout but cannot propose varied visual forms from a new design direction

steps.what: Check and refine adapted designs for wearability, construction and market suitability
Save the author's refined concept drawings

tasks.design: First test native templates and drawing tools in the {OTHER} garment-design system. Where rough concept variation still takes time, add a bounded image-draft loop from the designer's own adaptation direction; retain source assessment, market choices, construction refinement and ordinary author saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Visual exploration is slow, but an appealing image does not establish originality, wearability or manufacturability.
tasks.enabler_now: Image drafting can propose rough visual alternatives that the designer edits and rejects.
tasks.still_hard: Construction detail, material behaviour and the distinction between inspiration and imitation need judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The designer creates a coherent original adaptation that fits real customers and production limits.

ambition.what: Show a small set of alternative silhouettes during internal collection concept review

tasks.altitude: Some rough image drafting may shrink; final design choices and production responsibility stay with the designer.

reach.task: Refine visual concepts against manufacturing constraints
reach.learn: Separate concept imagery from production-ready specifications

evidence.claim: Adobe Creative Studio generates and edits images with Content Credentials; this supports rough image drafting, not garment construction or a measured saving for adaptation.

assumptions: Boundary is internal mass-market concept adaptation, not production pattern generation, publication or copying another designer's finished work. No release or supplier send is added.

The designer produces target customer, price, silhouette goals and construction constraints from the actual brief in s1-s3. The adaptation direction is first written in s3; no automatic understanding of a reference image is assumed.

Test native drawing templates before the model. Only six of thirty rough-drawing hours are removed; twenty-four remain for prompting, drawing, editing and checking generated meaning. All nineteen construction and wearability refinement hours remain, including manual fallback after failed drafts.

Author saves stay one fully retained hour and have no approval gate. Only authorised references are supplied, and available generation metadata remains with draft assets. Any new internal review service is an ambition, not an invented current baseline.
unknowns: Whether rough generated images are useful for the collection's style
Actual correction time for construction errors
research_questions: Do image drafts reduce rough sketching after counting edits and rejecting unusable construction details?

already_counted.description: Review and edit rough images, then refine construction and market suitability

incremental.description: Check draft-image failures, reference use and metadata retention after tool changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central: six rough-drawing hours removed less 1.5 upkeep gives 4.5. Cautious case: the collection requires precise stitch and construction annotations that rough images cannot preserve, so all thirty drawing hours remain and the image loop is not deployed or maintained. Source judgement, adaptation direction, refinement and saving remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Shows, materials, sourcing and design judgement remain personal work. Native source and stock views may remove small navigation costs; rough concept imagery has a limited, checked role.
reach: Commercial and industrial designer: test concepts against material and production constraints
Set and exhibit designer: source and inspect physical design items
skills_to_grow: Critical editing of concept images and construction feasibility
role.ambitious_version: A designer who explores a few more viable visual directions while staying grounded in physical materials, source context and production reality.
